//Logging: Both non-default levels below are load-bearing security settings, not tidiness, because this site's /angebot/{token} URL *is* a customer credential (Architecture.md §12). Microsoft.AspNetCore: ASP.NET's hosting diagnostics log every request line at Information, so raising this writes live tokens into every log sink; the API's appsettings.json holds the same level for the same reason. System.Net.Http.HttpClient: IHttpClientFactory's own handlers log 'Sending HTTP request GET {uri}' at Information, and every URI this Website requests contains the token — that category sits outside Microsoft.AspNetCore, so the first setting does not cover it. Program.cs also calls RemoveAllLoggers() on the typed client, which is the structural fix; this level is defence in depth. NOTE: these notes live OUTSIDE the Logging section on purpose. Logging:LogLevel is enumerated as category-to-level pairs, so every key under it must parse as a LogLevel and a '//' comment key there throws at startup. The '//' convention is only safe in sections bound with .Get<T>(), which ignores unknown keys.

PublicApi.//: Where this Website reaches the RenoTrack API. Deployment-specific, so no value is committed; the Development value is supplied through Properties/launchSettings.json, which is tracked and machine-independent. Required, and validated as an absolute HTTPS URL: the customer's token travels in this request's path.
PublicApi.//TimeoutSeconds: How long one API call may take before the customer sees the 'temporarily unavailable' page. Defaults to 10 if absent — unlike BaseUrl, a timeout has a safe default, which is the policy itself.

CompanyIdentity.//: Customer-facing company identity. No value is committed and none is invented (Phase 11 Q7): the real name and contact details are supplied before the completion gate, as Email:FromAddress and TokenLink:PublicBaseUrl already are. Absence is a startup warning, not a failure — this is copy, not wiring, and the page omits the heading rather than showing a placeholder a customer might mistake for a real name.

Legal.//: The two legally required German pages (SRS FR-1.4, ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D100). No text is committed and none is invented (Phase 11 Q7): the company authors it (SRS §5) and supplies it per deployment, here or through any other configuration source — an additional JSON file, environment variables, a mounted secret. A document with no content makes its route answer 404 and renders no link to it, which is deliberate: an empty page that looks like a legal page is worse than none. Absence logs one startup warning per document; a half-specified link (LinkUrl without LinkText, or the reverse) or a link using a scheme outside http/https/mailto/tel FAILS startup naming the key, because Razor encodes an attribute value but does not refuse 'javascript:'.

TrustedForwarders.//: The proxies whose X-Forwarded-* headers this Website believes (ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md D97). Empty means trust nothing, which is the default and the safe one: an unconfigured deployment behaves exactly as it did before D97 rather than believing a header any caller can set. Populate with the real reverse proxy at deployment time. KnownNetworks entries must be the canonical network address for their prefix: '10.0.0.1/8' is refused at startup rather than silently widened to '10.0.0.0/8' (System.Net.IPNetwork normalises rather than rejecting, contrary to its own documentation). To trust a single host, use KnownProxies.
